s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive systemic illness with unintentional weight loss and fatigue, accompanied by pancytopenia and a cardiac mass
salient_findings: Months of fatigue and 20-pound unintentional weight loss
Pancytopenia with subsequent recovery of all cell lines
Cardiac mass encasing the mid-right coronary artery
key_facts: 83-year-old man
History of colon cancer treated with surgery and 5-fluorouracil
History of squamous cell carcinoma of the right palatine tonsil treated with radiation
History of squamous cell carcinoma and basal cell carcinoma of the skin
Family history of various cancers without clear genetic cause
Initial laboratory evaluation revealed new pancytopenia
Complete blood count showed pancytopenia with subsequent recovery
Peripheral blood smear showed no peripheral blasts or abnormal B or T cells
Flow cytometry of tissue blasts was positive for CD13, CD34, CD38, and CD117
Cardiac MRI showed a mass with heterogeneous signal intensity and postcontrast enhancement
Transthoracic echocardiogram showed a mass within the right atrium causing restricted anterior tricuspid leaflet motion and mild tricuspid stenosis
Endomyocardial biopsy showed 80% tissue blast cells

shortlist.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Flow cytometry of tissue blasts was positive for CD13, CD34, CD38, and CD117, and endomyocardial biopsy showed 80% tissue blast cells

shortlist.label: Cardiac Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cardiac MRI showed a mass with heterogeneous signal intensity and postcontrast enhancement, and transthoracic echocardiogram showed a mass within the right atrium causing restricted anterior tricuspid leaflet motion and mild tricuspid stenosis

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of various cancers and presence of a cardiac mass, which could be a manifestation of lymphoma

shortlist.label: Metastatic Disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of colon cancer, squamous cell carcinoma of the right palatine tonsil, and other cancers, which increases the risk of metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Myeloproliferative Neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Pancytopenia with subsequent recovery and presence of blast cells on endomyocardial biopsy, which could be indicative of a myeloproliferative neoplasm

raw.rationale: The presence of pancytopenia, subsequent recovery of all cell lines, and flow cytometry of tissue blasts positive for CD13, CD34, CD38, and CD117, along with the endomyocardial biopsy showing 80% tissue blast cells, strongly supports the diagnosis of Acute Myeloid Leukemia, particularly given the involvement of the heart which can be a site for extramedullary disease in AML.

rejected.label: Cardiac Sarcoma
rejected.why: While the cardiac MRI and echocardiogram show a mass within the right atrium, the presence of blast cells in the endomyocardial biopsy and the specific immunophenotypic markers (CD13, CD34, CD38, CD117) point more towards a hematological malignancy like AML rather than a primary cardiac sarcoma.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: The peripheral blood smear showed no abnormal B or T cells, and the flow cytometry of tissue blasts was positive for myeloid markers (CD13, CD34, CD38, CD117), which does not support a diagnosis of lymphoma.

rejected.label: Metastatic Disease
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of various cancers, the specific findings of blast cells in the endomyocardial biopsy and the immunophenotypic markers suggest a primary hematological malignancy rather than metastasis from a previous cancer.

rejected.label: Myeloproliferative Neoplasm
rejected.why: The presence of pancytopenia and the specific blast cell markers (CD13, CD34, CD38, CD117) are more indicative of an acute leukemia rather than a myeloproliferative neoplasm, which typically presents with an overproduction of one or more myeloid cell lines without significant blast cell population.
